incident.counterexampleWrapper: contract OracleCounterexample is OmrV4TwapOracleTest { function test_exact_CI_counterexample() public { testFuzz_no_prepool_or_prebaseline_time_qualifies(4294967295, 17160, 25, true); } }
incident.cause: The second arbitrary delay left the initialized source without a persisted checkpoint for uint32.max seconds. The oracle seeded immediately before the source elapsed counter wrapped. During the otherwise valid 1800-second oracle window the source counterfactual cumulative then dropped. Mock and real Hook both use uint32 elapsed since the last persisted source checkpoint; observer notifications do not persist that checkpoint. This is not a false positive for an unlimited-idle source guarantee.

correction.testChange: Keep both arbitrary delays and all original oracle assertions. Split the initialized-history delay into floor(delay/2) and the remainder, persisting the same tick after each interval; both intervals are at most uint32.max for the unchanged delay range. Assert the full cumulative equals tick * fullDelay and the baseline captures it. Add exact-input deterministic tests for both observer and direct-update seeding.
preservedProperties: No pre-pool or initialized prebaseline time qualifies toward the first quote
The entire arbitrary initialized history is accumulated, including delays exceeding one uint32 wrap
The first quote remains unavailable at baseline and before PERIOD
Early direct updates revert with the expected PeriodNotElapsed arguments
One full fresh PERIOD yields the unchanged tick and a fresh positive quote
Delay bounds [0, 2*uint32.max], tick bounds [-100000,100000] and early bounds [0,PERIOD-1] are unchanged
correction.sourceModelAssumption: Each persisted source interval must fit uint32 elapsed. A same-tick mock setTick write models the real Hook accumulator write after a successful swap with unchanged tick; it is not a new keeper capability. pokeObserver does not update the Hook accumulator.

findings.status: open residual risk; unchanged production behavior
findings.classification: Real source horizon limitation, not a dismissed fuzz false positive
findings.prerequisites: An initialized pool source has no persisted tick accumulator write for nearly 2^32 seconds (roughly 136 years), then an otherwise valid oracle window crosses that source elapsed wrap.
findings.impact: The reproduced source cumulative discontinuity causes InvalidTick(7456565), so the first quote cannot be published for that window. Source correctness beyond the no-write uint32 horizon is not established; the test correction does not repair this production limitation.
findings.severityRationale: The observed failure requires approximately 136 years without a source write. No active chain rail is changed or activated by this backend release; immediate production exploitability or economic loss is not claimed.
findings.disposition: Retained as a pre-chain risk. A production source horizon policy or fix requires separate review before any claim of unlimited-idle reliability. The corrected bootstrap property assumes faithful persisted checkpoints within the representable source interval.

conclusion: The scoped bootstrap test now exercises complete arbitrary historical accumulation under the source representability assumption, then independently proves a fresh full oracle period is required. The exact failing CI input passes for both baseline entry points; all 25 oracle tests pass under both fixed seeds (16,384 total fuzz executions). Production Solidity is unchanged. The full impacted contract CI gate is still required; this package does not claim complete repository audit coverage or chain activation readiness.
